events.title: Tarquinius Priscus celebrates a triumph over the Sabines
events.description: Lucius Tarquinius Priscus, by Roman tradition the fifth king of Rome, celebrated a triumph after defeating the Sabines, who ceded the town of Collatia in the peace that followed. The story belongs to the semi-legendary period before the Republic.

events.title: The Temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill is dedicated
events.description: According to Livy, the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus on Rome's Capitoline Hill was dedicated on the Ides of September in the Republic's first year, by the consul Marcus Horatius Pulvillus. Dionysius of Halicarnassus dated the consecration to 507 BCE.

events.title: Khosrow I becomes Sasanian King of Kings
events.description: Khosrow I, known as Anushirvan, succeeded his father Kavad I as Sasanian King of Kings and went on to negotiate an end to the Iberian War with the Byzantine Empire. He reigned until 579 and reformed taxation and the army.

events.title: Belisarius defeats the Vandal king Gelimer at Ad Decimum
events.description: At the tenth milestone south of Carthage, the Byzantine general Belisarius defeated the Vandal army of King Gelimer, whose attempt to trap the invaders failed. Belisarius entered Carthage two days later, opening Justinian I's reconquest of North Africa.

events.title: Sabinian is consecrated pope, succeeding Gregory the Great
events.description: Sabinian was consecrated bishop of Rome, succeeding Pope Gregory I, who had died in March. A former apocrisiarius to Constantinople, he reigned during the Eastern Roman domination of the papacy until his death in February 606.

events.title: Wolfe defeats Montcalm on the Plains of Abraham
events.description: British troops under James Wolfe climbed the cliffs above Quebec and defeated the French in a brief battle. Wolfe was killed and Montcalm mortally wounded; Quebec fell, sealing Britain's conquest of Canada.

events.title: The British bombard Fort McHenry in Baltimore
events.description: British warships shelled Fort McHenry for some 25 hours. Seeing the flag still flying at dawn, Francis Scott Key wrote the poem that became 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.

events.title: Rabin and Arafat shake hands on the Oslo Accords
events.description: Israel and the PLO signed the Declaration of Principles at the White House, with a historic handshake between Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat. The deal created Palestinian self-rule, but lasting peace proved elusive.

events.title: Tupac Shakur dies after a drive-by shooting
events.description: Rapper Tupac Shakur died in Las Vegas aged 25, six days after being shot. One of hip-hop's best-selling and most influential artists, his murder long went unsolved.
